g.title: Anonymous Internet Attacker no account or prior foothold SQL and shell injection reads data, runs commands I send POST /vulnerabilities/api/v2/health/connectivity with JSON body {"target":"x; id"}, without any token. C-03 · DVWA API service No account required Application data builds operating-system commands (W-001) Technical consequence not established. Service disruption or compromise of application data Disclosure of customer information
g.text: SQL and shell injection reads data,

g.title: Anonymous Internet Attacker no account or prior foothold Bypass or Forge Authentication Session tokens are JSON encrypted with AES-128-ECB under a hardcoded key and have no MAC. An attacker splices 16-byte blocks from captured tokens, for example Sweep's user field with Sooty's admin level and a valid expiry, and submits the forged token to be accepted as admin Sweep. C-03 · DVWA API service No account required Security-sensitive data uses weak cryptographic primitives (W-005) Technical consequence not established. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data

Anonymous Internet Attacker no account or prior foothold Bypass Authorization to Gain Access An authenticated user sets the user_id cookie to another user's ID and requests that ID; the server compares the request ID with the cookie and returns the other user's profile. C-03 · DVWA API service No account required No weakness linked in the register Technical consequence not established. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data

Anonymous Internet Attacker no account or prior foothold Execute Attacker-Controlled Server Code At vulnerabilities/view_help.php:20, view_help.php builds a path from the unsanitised id and locale parameters, reads vulnerabilities/{id}/help/help.php (or help.{locale}.php), and evals the contents as PHP. An authenticated user sets id to a traversal such as ../../some/dir. Any reachable help.php or locale-matching file that the attacker can place or select then runs as server-side code. The page requires a DVWA login (line 6), but there is no allowlist on id or locale and no path containment. C-03 · DVWA API service No account required Application data crosses into executable code (W-006) Technical consequence not established. Service disruption or compromise of application data Disclosure of customer information Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data

Authenticated Internet Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Bypass or Forge Authentication I open /login.php and read the anti-CSRF token from the form. C-04 · DVWA web application Regular account required; Source-repository access required Secrets are committed to source instead of a managed store (W-004) Technical consequence not established. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data

Authenticated Internet Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Access Exposed Data and Secrets At vulnerabilities/view_source.php:63 the unvalidated id and security GET values are joined into a file_get_contents path ending in .php, and the file is echoed with highlight_string. Any logged-in DVWA user passes dvwaPageStartup(array('authenticated')). The user then requests view_source.php?id=sqli or id=fi with security=../../../config/config.inc to escape the source directory. This discloses any .php file the web server can read, such as config.inc.php with its database credentials. The switch on id only sets a label, and its default branch accepts any value. C-03 · DVWA API service Regular account required Input handling lacks enforced boundary validation (W-002) Technical consequence not established. Disclosure of customer information

Supply-Chain / Build Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Compromise the Build or Its Inputs At compose.yml:31 the MariaDB root password and the dvwa application user password are written as literals in the service environment. Anyone who can read the repository learns them, and every deployment that uses compose.yml unchanged shares the same known credentials. An attacker who reaches the db service, for example from another container on the dvwa network or from a compromised app container, can log in as root and read or change all application data. The db service publishes no host ports and sits only on the internal dvwa network, and the web port is bound to 127.0.0.1 (line 25). C-02 · CI/CD Pipeline Build or dependency access required; Source-repository access required Secrets are committed to source instead of a managed store (W-004) Technical consequence not established. Service disruption or compromise of application data
g.text: Compromise the Build or Its Inputs
